title: Tomato Chutney

instruction.title: Prepare the Tomatoes
steps: Bring a pot of water to a boil.
Blanch the tomatoes for 2–3 minutes until their skins begin to split.
Remove the tomatoes and allow them to cool slightly.
Peel off the skins and chop the tomatoes finely.

instruction.title: Temper the Spices
steps: Heat the refined oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add mustard seeds and allow them to crackle.
Add fenugreek seeds, broken dry red chilies, and curry leaves.
Fry for 5–7 seconds, taking care not to burn the fenugreek seeds.

instruction.title: Build the Flavor Base
steps: Add the sliced onions and sauté until soft and lightly golden.
Add grated ginger, minced garlic, and slit green chilies.
Cook until the raw aroma disappears and the aromatics become fragrant.

instruction.title: Cook the Chutney
steps: Add turmeric powder and Kashmiri red chili powder.
Stir briefly to bloom the spices without burning them.
Add the blanched chopped tomatoes and salt.
Cook over medium heat for 10–12 minutes until the tomatoes soften and the oil begins to separate.
Add jaggery and tamarind pulp if using.
Stir well and cook for another 3–4 minutes until the chutney thickens to a glossy consistency.

instruction.title: Finish & Store
steps: Taste and adjust the salt, sweetness, and tang as needed.
Allow the chutney to cool completely before transferring it to clean, sterilized jars.
Refrigerate for up to 2 weeks.

instruction.title: Serve
steps: Serve with dosa, idli, chapati, or pakoras.
Use as a tangy spread for sandwiches and wraps.

chefTips: Tomatoes: Blanching and peeling the tomatoes creates a smoother, richer chutney texture.
Oil separation: Visible oil separation is a useful sign that the tomatoes and spices have cooked down properly.
Fenugreek: Use fenugreek sparingly and fry it only briefly, as burnt or excessive fenugreek can make the chutney bitter.
Balance: Adjust jaggery and tamarind according to the natural acidity of the tomatoes.
Storage: Refrigerate in a clean airtight container for up to 2 weeks. For longer storage, use properly sterilized jars and ensure an oil layer covers the surface.
Serving: The chutney works especially well as an accompaniment to South Indian breakfasts and as a spicy-tangy sandwich spread.
